source_read: Saved publisher page text (SAGE, free access; Aust N Z J Psychiatry 2018;52(6):514–529), read in full: structured abstract, Introduction, Method, Results with Tables 1–2 (as text), Discussion, Conclusion, declarations and funding. Figures 1–2 are images; the online appendices were not available.

anchors.locator: Results › Dose-amount and frequency of MA use; Table 2 (Frequency of use rows)
anchors.extracted: More frequent use was associated with psychosis in 4 populations (1503 participants) and not in 4 (2503), with odds 3 to 11 times higher in more frequent users; in the one prospective within-person cohort (McKetin et al., 2013), which controlled for other drug use, use on 16 or more days a month gave OR 11.2 (95% CI 5.9–21.1), which the review describes as against use on fewer than 16 days.
anchors.note: The comparator matters: the encyclopedia's card for McKetin et al. (2013), read from the publisher's full text, gives 11.2 for months of 16–28 days of use against months of no use (1–15 days against no use: 4.0), so the review's comparator appears to be a misdescription (now card reporting issue 8). The other numbers are confirmed.

anchors.locator: Table 1 (quality column, study 4, and footnote b: +++ = total score 11–13); Table 2 (Frequency of use rows)
anchors.note: Data right: McKetin et al. (2013, 2016; study 4) is the only population rated +++, and frequency was associated with psychosis in 4 of the 8 populations that examined it. The 'Risk of bias within studies' paragraph gives only the score range (5 to 12, mean 7.85) and does not mention bands.

not_added: Table 2's personality row says two studies found an association with schizoid/schizotypal traits but cites one study (study 6) and comments that only one assessed it: confirmed; minor, and no claim relies on it.

The review compares people with and without psychosis who all use methamphetamine, so it cannot support user-versus-non-user odds ratios: already stated in cannot_establish and comparison; a matter for cl_meth_psychosis_association.
